overview: A five-page Department of State “List of Papers” index, on a form marked October 12, 1945, summarizing and cross-referencing items 492–534 filed under Japanese merchant vessels. The entries, dating chiefly from 1931–1938, trace the effects of the Chinese boycott, the Manchurian Incident, and the British gold embargo; expansion and regulation of Japan’s merchant marine; shipping competition and new routes; shipbuilding, subsidies, and cargo-preference policies; and the activities of major Japanese shipping companies. The later entries concern the attempted bombing of the HIYE/HIYEI MARU at Seattle, measures to protect Japanese vessels in American ports, monthly shipping reports, and Japan’s growing wartime transport requirements. The file contains the archival index rather than the underlying telegrams, despatches, memoranda, letters, and clippings to which it refers.

subfiles.title: List of Papers: Merchant Vessels—Japan, entries 492–534
subfiles.about: An archival index summarizes and cross-references State Department papers on Japanese merchant shipping, maritime policy, trade routes, and vessel security from 1931 through 1938.
subfiles.summary: The list records items 492–534, with no item 515 shown, and gives their senders, dates, routing symbols, brief purports, and references to related decimal files. Early entries address shipping losses, foreign competition, fleet expansion, ship purchases, new routes, and the 1936 law controlling sea routes. Later entries cover government influence over shipbuilding and cargo carriage, the attempted bombing of the HIYE MARU at Seattle, protection of Japanese ships in American ports, and monthly shipping conditions in the Japanese Empire. The final entries describe subsidies for small merchant vessels, increased traffic between Japan and China, prospective Yangtze operations, and consolidation of shipping interests linking Japan, northern Korea, and Manchukuo.

interest: Shows 1930s US tracking of Japan's shipping expansion, including a bombing attempt on a Japanese liner at Seattle.
